+# 丘 — hill; knoll
+
+**Strokes:** 5 · **Key (radical):** 一 (the long bottom horizontal, no. 1) · **JLPT:** N1 (community list)
+
+## Meaning and origin
+
+丘 means a hill or knoll: land rising above its surroundings. The native noun is [丘](../words/丘.md) おか. A hill is typically lower and gentler than a mountain, but these everyday labels do not impose a universal numerical height boundary.
+
+**Modern-shape mnemonic, not etymology:** Imagine the short slant and upright strokes as a small rise standing on the long ground line. This is a visual memory aid, not a historical explanation of the character.
+
+## Readings
+
+| Reading | Type | Typical words |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| キュウ | on | [砂丘](../words/砂丘.md) さきゅう - sand dune |
+| おか | kun | [丘](../words/丘.md) おか - hill; rising ground |
+
+Both sourced readings are selected for practice. Learn the whole word: 砂丘 is さきゅう, not すなおか.
+
+## Common words
+
+- [丘](../words/丘.md) おか - hill; rising ground
+- [砂丘](../words/砂丘.md) さきゅう - sand dune
+
+## Notes
+
+- [山](山.md) means mountain and can also describe a hill in context. [坂](坂.md) focuses on a slope or inclined road; it can be part of a hill.
+- 岡 is another dictionary spelling of the native noun おか. Do not assume that every name containing either spelling is read おか.
+- Distinguish the five-stroke 丘 from [兵](兵.md), soldier or troops: 兵 has two spreading strokes below its upper part, rather than 丘's long bottom horizontal.
+

+# 砂丘 (さきゅう) - sand dune
+
+## Meaning
+
+砂丘 is a sand dune: a raised accumulation of sand formed by wind. Dunes occur not only in deserts but also along coasts and in other sandy settings.
+
+- 砂丘を歩きました。 (さきゅうをあるきました。) - We walked across the sand dunes.
+- 砂丘の上から海が見えます。 (さきゅうのうえからうみがみえます。) - You can see the sea from the top of the dune.
+
+In the first example, を marks the area traversed. In the second, から gives the viewpoint. Japanese does not require the noun to distinguish one dune from several.
+
+## How the kanji combine
+
+[砂](../kanji/砂.md) contributes sand and [丘](../kanji/丘.md) contributes hill: a modifier-plus-head combination, "a hill of sand." The on readings here are サ + キュウ, giving さきゅう.
+
+JMdict also lists しゃきゅう for this word; this card uses さきゅう. The alternative spelling 沙丘 is marked as irregular kanji usage. These are dictionary alternatives, not a rule for changing サ to シャ in every compound.
+
+## Synonyms and antonyms
+
+[丘](丘.md) (おか) is a hill without specifying its material. [砂](砂.md) (すな) is the sand itself, not the landform. [砂漠](砂漠.md) (さばく) is a desert region, not an individual dune; a desert need not be covered in dunes. 砂浜 (すなはま) is a sandy beach. These are related geographical words, not exact synonyms or a set of antonyms.
+
+## Distinctive meaning
+
+Use 砂丘 for the raised sandy landform, not any patch or grain of sand. A coastal dune can stand near a beach without the two words naming the same feature.
+
+Sources: [JMdict](https://www.edrdg.org/wiki/index.php/JMdict-EDICT_Dictionary_Project), entry 1291520; [砂丘 (さきゅう), encyclopedia article](https://kotobank.jp/word/%E7%A0%82%E4%B8%98-68650).
